{{Quote|We have deployed a technician with a special task force to reacquire the droid control program.|Nute Gunray to OOM-9|audio=WeTechThose.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
A [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] '''technician''' worked for the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. He was part of a small task force sent to retrieve a stolen [[droid control program]] from a [[Research Center]] near the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Harte Secur]]. After regaining the program, the [[Technician/Legends|technician]] was able to reactivate a portion of the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|You must protect the technician at all costs!|Nute Gunray's orders to OOM-9|audio=TechObjective.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
[[File:The_magnificent_seven.png|thumb|right|250px|The technician (bottom left) with the task force]]
A [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]]<ref name="GB" /> [[Technician/Legends|technician]] was used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] during their [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The technician was included in a specialist task force along with five [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] and a [[bio cannon]], which was charged with [[Capture of Harte Secur|retrieving]] a [[droid control program]] that had been stolen by the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] and taken to a [[Research Center]] near the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Harte Secur]]. The task force was deployed via a [[Neimoidian transport]] to a [[Deactivated Camp|camp]] filled with [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] deactivated by the loss of the program, where they met with the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]].<ref name="GB" />

[[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] ordered OOM-9 to retrieve the program and protect the technician. The Neimoidian was loaded inside OOM-9's personal [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Heavy Armored Assault Tank]] for protection while the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] fought through groups of [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] to reach the research center. Once there, the technician retrieved the program and the task force returned to the camp, where he was able to reactivate the droids. The technician then remained inside the camp's [[command center]] while the Droid Army destroyed Harte Secur.<ref name="Prima" />

==Personality and traits==
The Neimoidian technician had [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and mottled green skin.<ref name="GB" />

==Skills and abilities==
The technician was capable of reactivating a portion of the Trade Federation Droid Army after reacquiring a droid control program.<ref name="GB" />

==Equipment==
The Neimoidian wore blue and gray [[Robe/Legends|robes]] along with a dark blue [[Hat/Legends|hat]].<ref name="GB" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:GalacticBattlegrounds.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds'', the video game the Neimoidian technician first appears in]]
The Neimoidian technician was first mentioned in the [[Prima Games]]' [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] by [[Steven L. Kent]]<ref name="Prima" />&mdash;released on [[November 7]], [[2001]]<ref name="PrimaDate">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Galactic-Battlegrounds-Official/dp/0761537503|text=Star Wars Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide}}</ref>&mdash;for the [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'',<ref name="GB" /> released on [[November 11]], 2001.<ref name="GBDate">{{GameSpot|url=games/star-wars-galactic-battlegrounds|text=Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds}}</ref> He appears in the second level of the Trade Federation campaign, "Behind the Lines." Losing the technician causes the player to automatically lose the level, even after they have retrieved the program.<ref name="GB" />

The strategy guide compares the technician to the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] in the game, as the technician is the only unit able to move the droid control program, similar to how only Jedi and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] can move [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]]. The guide also recommends [[Garrison/Legends|garrisoning]] the technician inside OOM-9's AAT, which allows the droid control program to be collected by moving the AAT over it.<ref name="Prima" /> In the level, if the player sends the technician near the program outside of the AAT, the program disappears, only reappearing once the technician returns to the camp.<ref name="GB" />
